primary_claim: A per-layer linear-probe map of where a syntactic/semantic signal (POS, NER, chunking) is built in BERT-family encoders predicts where quantization damage lands, and using this map to guide per-layer bit allocation preserves 99-100% of full-precision accuracy at a 5-bit average budget on three datasets never used to build the map, versus 16-41% for uniform quantization and 2-41% for anti/opposite-layer allocation, with the same pattern replicating on a decoder LLM (Qwen2.5-3B), where the guided split preserves F1 down to about 3 bits per layer on average versus uniform needing about 8.

effect.metric: accuracy retained at a 5-bit average budget on unseen datasets, guided vs uniform vs anti/opposite layer allocation
effect.value: guided: 99-100% (100% web-text POS, 99% tweet NER, 100% WSJ chunks); uniform: 16-41%; anti/opposite: 2-41%; on Qwen2.5-3B, guided split preserves F1 down to ~3 bits/layer average vs uniform needing ~8 bits

contradicts_or_qualifies: notes Q-BERT, HAWQ, and HAQ also choose layers to protect for quantization but require Hessians or hardware search, whereas this probe-guided approach needs only a few seconds of a RidgeClassifier per layer

confirms Tenney et al.'s finding that BERT builds syntactic structure before entity information and shows this ordering generalises across BERT, BERT-large, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT even as exact peak layers shift
stated_future_work: extend the probe-guided approach to pruning, distillation, or dropping layers entirely
develop a way to tell in advance which trait/signal a given task will lean on, currently a judgment call by the user
limitations_stated: only tested on one encoder family (BERT and relatives) and one decoder LLM (Qwen2.5-3B), one seed, token-level tasks, and post-training weight quantization
unclear whether the method holds when the task is diffuse, like general-knowledge QA (probably not)
does not benefit diffuse/general-intelligence tasks like the ARC challenge, and there is no way to tell in advance which trait the model will lean on for such a task
an unexplained result: both the anti and uniform strategies kept the same 41% accuracy on WNUT
quote: a map built once on CoNLL news keeps 99–100% of full-precision accuracy at a 5-bit average on three unseen datasets, whereas Uniform kept 16–41% and opposite/anti layers kept 2–41%.
